problemSection.headline: If money in the bank felt like enough, you wouldn't be reading this.
problemSection.p1: So you wait. Month after month. And slowly… your money loses value because of rising prices.
problemSection.p2: And every cousin with a smartphone says "Da, SIP ma paisa halnus na" — but when you open one of those apps, it asks about your "risk profile" and "asset allocation," shows you 3,000 funds, and you close the app.
problemSection.notProblem: You are not the problem. The apps are.
problemSection.s1: You don't need 3,000 funds. You need one good one, started simply.
problemSection.s2: You don't need to predict the market. You just need to stay in it.
problemSection.s3: You don't need to be a 'finance person.' You just need someone honest to walk you through Day 1.
problemSection.whatWeAreHereFor: That is what we are here for.

objectionSection.label: Honest answers
objectionSection.headline: What you might be thinking right now
objectionSection.a1: Yes — for someone trying to make a quick buck in 6 months. No — for someone investing ₹100 a day for 10 years. SIPs work because they buy more units when prices fall, fewer when prices rise. Volatility is the engine, not the enemy. We just automate it.
objectionSection.a2: That's okay. Most people don't. That's why EazySip is simple. We guide you like a friend would.
objectionSection.q3: "How much money do I need to start?"
objectionSection.a3: ₹100. That's it. No upfront fees. No "minimum balance." No hidden charges. Increase later if you want.
objectionSection.q4: "What if I lose all the money?"
objectionSection.a4: On any single day, your investment may be up or down — that's normal. Over 10+ years, equity mutual funds in India have averaged around 12% annually. Your job is just to stay in. Our job is to remind you why.
objectionSection.a5: Yes. Any time. No notice period for most funds. Withdrawals reach your bank in 1–3 working days. It is your money. We never forget that.
objectionSection.a6: Fair question. The money is never held by us — it gets directly parked with reputed mutual fund companies. If we ever stop being worth your trust, you walk away with your money.

faqSection.label: FAQ
faqSection.headline: Questions first-time investors actually ask
faqSection.a1: Yes. EazySip is a SEBI-registered platform. Your money never sits with us — it moves directly from your bank to the mutual fund company. We earn nothing if you don't invest, and we never take commissions from fund houses.
faqSection.a2: No upfront fees, no "premium account," no commissions. The fund house charges its standard expense ratio (typically 0.3–0.8% per year).
faqSection.q3: What if I want to stop my SIP?
faqSection.a3: Pause it for free, any time. No phone calls, no penalty. Restart whenever you're ready. Your past investment continues to grow even if you pause.
faqSection.q4: Do I need to be tech-savvy?
faqSection.a4: No. If you can use WhatsApp, you can use EazySip. We have voice notes in Nepali if reading is hard, and a real human you can talk to.
faqSection.q5: How is this different from an FD?
faqSection.a5: FD pays around 6–7% — inflation eats most of it. Equity mutual funds, over 10+ years, have averaged around 12%. FD is safer for 1 year. SIPs are smarter for 10. EazySip helps you hold the SIP long enough for the second part to matter.
faqSection.q6: Can I withdraw money if I have an emergency?
faqSection.a6: Yes — any time. Withdrawals usually reach your bank in 1–3 working days. There is no exit fee for most funds we use.
faqSection.a7: Mostly first-time investors aged 21–50, with monthly incomes between ₹15,000 and ₹60,000. People who would rather start small and stay long, than start big and stop scared. People exactly like you.
faqSection.msgUs: Message us in Nepali, Hindi, or English on WhatsApp. A real person — not a bot — replies between 8 AM and 10 PM.

learn.heroHeadline: Your Guide to Understanding Mutual Funds
learn.heroSubtitle: From basics to advanced — understand mutual funds at your own pace.

featured.title: Why is investing better than saving?
featured.excerpt: Saving keeps your money safe, but investing makes it grow. With inflation eating into savings, staying invested in mutual funds is the only way to build real wealth over time.

articles.title: What is a Mutual Fund?
articles.excerpt: A mutual fund pools money from many investors to buy a diversified portfolio of stocks, bonds, or other securities.

articles.title: Why invest through Mutual Funds instead of Fixed Deposits?
articles.excerpt: Fixed deposits offer fixed but low returns. Mutual funds, especially equity ones, have historically delivered returns that beat inflation over the long run.

articles.title: What is the power of compounding?
articles.excerpt: Compounding means your returns earn returns. Starting early even with small amounts can lead to significant wealth over 10–20 years.

articles.title: How can Mutual Funds help create wealth?
articles.excerpt: By investing regularly in equity funds over a long period, you benefit from market growth, compounding, and professional fund management.

articles.title: What is an Asset Management Company (AMC)?
articles.excerpt: An AMC is a company that collects money from investors and invests it in various assets on their behalf, managed by experienced fund managers.

articles.title: How to get started with Mutual Fund investments?
articles.excerpt: Complete your KYC, choose a goal, pick a fund that matches your risk appetite, and start a SIP. eazySIP makes this possible in your language.

articles.title: What is a SIP and how does it work?
articles.excerpt: A SIP lets you invest a fixed amount every month automatically. It builds discipline, removes the need to time the market, and benefits from rupee-cost averaging.

articles.title: Why is SIP better than lump sum investing?
articles.excerpt: SIP spreads your investment across market cycles, reducing risk. You don't need a large sum upfront — even ₹100/month can build a significant corpus.

articles.title: What is the cost of delaying your SIP by 5 years?
articles.excerpt: Delaying a ₹5,000/month SIP by just 5 years can cost you ₹25–30 lakh in final corpus. The earlier you start, the more compounding works for you.

articles.title: What is a Step-Up SIP?
articles.excerpt: A Step-Up SIP automatically increases your monthly investment amount by a fixed percentage each year, helping you invest more as your income grows.

articles.title: What is a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP)?
articles.excerpt: An SWP lets you withdraw a fixed amount from your mutual fund every month — ideal for generating regular income in retirement.

articles.title: Should I risk my savings in Mutual Funds?
articles.excerpt: All investments carry some risk, but mutual funds are diversified and regulated by SEBI. The risk is manageable and reduces significantly over a long investment horizon.

articles.title: Why should market volatility not bother you?
articles.excerpt: Short-term market dips are normal. SIP investors actually benefit from volatility through rupee-cost averaging — buying more units when prices fall.

articles.title: How do Mutual Funds help manage risk?
articles.excerpt: Mutual funds invest across many stocks and bonds, so poor performance of one company doesn't significantly impact your overall portfolio.

articles.title: Do equity and debt funds carry different risks?
articles.excerpt: Equity funds carry market risk but offer higher long-term returns. Debt funds are more stable but give lower returns. Choosing the right type depends on your goal and time horizon.

articles.title: What is Absolute Return?
articles.excerpt: Absolute return is the total percentage gain or loss on your investment from the day you invested, regardless of how long it took.

articles.title: What is XIRR and why does it matter?
articles.excerpt: XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return) gives the annualised return on investments with irregular cash flows like SIPs — it's the most accurate way to measure SIP returns.

articles.title: Mutual Funds vs Fixed Deposits: Which earns more?
articles.excerpt: Over 10+ years, equity mutual funds have historically given 12–15% annual returns vs 5–7% from FDs. After inflation and taxes, FD returns can even go negative.

articles.title: How soon can I withdraw from Mutual Funds?
articles.excerpt: Equity fund redemptions typically credit to your bank within 2–3 business days (T+2). Liquid funds credit on the same or next day.

articles.title: What costs do I pay when redeeming Mutual Fund units?
articles.excerpt: You may pay an exit load (typically 1% if redeemed within 1 year) and applicable taxes on capital gains depending on your holding period.

articles.title: What is Exit Load and when does it apply?
articles.excerpt: Exit load is a fee charged by the fund house if you redeem units before a specified period (usually 1 year for equity funds). It discourages short-term trading.

featured.title: How to build a retirement corpus with Mutual Funds?
featured.excerpt: Retirement can last 25–30 years. Starting a SIP in equity funds early, then gradually shifting to debt funds as you near retirement, is the proven strategy to build a large enough corpus.

articles.title: What are Equity Funds?
articles.excerpt: Equity funds invest primarily in stocks. They carry higher risk but offer the potential for higher long-term returns — ideal for goals 5+ years away.

articles.title: What are Debt Funds?
articles.excerpt: Debt funds invest in bonds and fixed-income instruments. They are more stable than equity funds and suit short-to-medium term goals.

articles.title: What are Index Funds?
articles.excerpt: Index funds passively track a market index like Nifty 50 or Sensex. They have very low expense ratios and are a great option for first-time investors.

articles.title: What are Hybrid Funds?
articles.excerpt: Hybrid funds invest in both equity and debt, offering a balance of growth and stability. They are ideal for moderate-risk investors.

articles.title: ETFs vs Mutual Funds: What's the difference?
articles.excerpt: ETFs trade on exchanges like stocks throughout the day, while mutual fund NAV is calculated once daily. Both have pros and cons depending on your investment style.

articles.title: Should I set a goal before starting a SIP?
articles.excerpt: Having a goal helps you pick the right fund, determine the right amount, and stay invested without panic-selling during market dips.

articles.title: Which fund should I choose for long-term goals (10+ years)?
articles.excerpt: For goals 10+ years away, diversified equity funds or index funds are generally recommended, as they have historically delivered the best inflation-beating returns.

articles.title: How do I plan for my child's education?
articles.excerpt: Education costs double every 8–10 years. Starting a SIP today in equity funds ensures you build enough corpus by the time your child is ready for college.

articles.title: Which fund is right for a mid-term goal (3–5 years)?
articles.excerpt: For goals 3–5 years away, balanced or hybrid funds, or aggressive debt funds like dynamic bond funds, offer a good mix of growth and stability.

articles.title: How to build a retirement corpus with Mutual Funds?
articles.excerpt: Start early with equity funds, gradually shift to debt as you approach retirement. Use an SWP to generate monthly income post-retirement.

articles.title: How much SIP do I need to retire comfortably?
articles.excerpt: Use our SIP calculator to estimate the monthly investment needed. As a rule of thumb, aim to build a corpus that generates monthly income equal to 70–80% of your pre-retirement salary.

articles.title: Why start retirement planning in your 30s?
articles.excerpt: Starting a ₹5,000/month SIP at age 30 can grow to ₹1.75 crore by age 60 (at 12% returns). Waiting until 40 gives only ₹50 lakh for the same investment.

sections.title: 1. Scope & Applicability
sections.body: This Privacy Policy applies to the EazySip website and mobile application (the "Platform") operated by Dzambala Financial Services LLP ("Dzambala", "we", "us"), and governs the collection, use, storage, sharing and protection of personal data of users, prospects, investors and their nominees/representatives ("you") who access the Platform. It supplements, and must be read with, the EazySip Website Disclaimer and Terms & Conditions.

sections.title: 2. Legal Framework
sections.body: We currently process personal data in accordance with the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 ("SPDI Rules"). We are also aligning our practices with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act"), whose substantive compliance obligations are being phased in under the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025; where a DPDP Act obligation is not yet in force, we follow it as a voluntary best practice pending statutory applicability.

sections.title: 3. Information We Collect
sections.body: We collect: (a) identity/KYC information (name, PAN, Aadhaar masked/reference number, photograph, signature, address proof); (b) contact details (mobile, email, postal address); (c) financial information (bank details, income/tax status, investment and transaction history, portfolio holdings), which is Sensitive Personal Data or Information under the SPDI Rules; (d) technical data (IP address, device ID, cookies, log files); and (e) your communications with our Sahayogis/support team.

sections.title: 4. Purpose & Lawful Basis
sections.body: Data is collected with your consent and/or as necessary to perform KYC/onboarding and distribution services, comply with SEBI/AMFI/PMLA/KRA obligations, process transactions, prevent fraud, and improve the Platform. Sensitive personal data is collected only where necessary for a lawful purpose connected with our functions.

sections.title: 5. Sharing & Disclosure
sections.body: Your data may be shared with AMCs, Registrars & Transfer Agents (CAMS, KFin Technologies), KYC Registration Agencies, payment gateways/UPI/banking partners, SEBI/AMFI/FIU-IND and other regulators/statutory authorities, and our auditors, cloud-hosting and IT service providers, strictly for the purposes stated in this Policy and under confidentiality obligations. We do not sell personal data to third parties for their independent marketing use.

sections.title: 6. Cross-Border Transfer
sections.body: Personal data may be processed on servers located in India or, where our cloud service providers so require, outside India, except to any country restricted by the Central Government under the DPDP Act.

sections.title: 7. Data Retention
sections.body: Records, including KYC and transaction data, are retained for the periods mandated under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 and applicable SEBI/AMFI recordkeeping norms (currently a minimum of five years from the end of the business relationship, or longer if directed by a regulator/court), and are erased or anonymised thereafter in line with the DPDP Act's purpose-limitation principle.

sections.title: 8. Security
sections.body: We maintain reasonable security practices and procedures, including encryption, access controls and a documented information-security policy, as required under the SPDI Rules and Section 43A of the IT Act. Cyber-security incidents are handled and reported to CERT-In within the timelines prescribed under the CERT-In Cyber Security Directions, 2022 (currently within 6 hours of notice, for reportable incidents). No system is completely secure; see also Limitation of Liability in the Website Disclaimer.

sections.title: 9. Your Rights
sections.body: Subject to applicable law, you may request access to, correction of, or erasure of your personal data, withdraw consent prospectively, nominate a representative to exercise your rights in the event of death/incapacity, and raise a grievance with our contact below; unresolved grievances may, once the relevant DPDP Act provisions are in force, be escalated to the Data Protection Board of India.

sections.title: 10. Cookies
sections.body: We use cookies and similar technologies to operate the Platform, remember preferences, and for analytics; you may control cookies through your browser settings, though some features may not function without them.

sections.title: 11. Children's Data
sections.body: The Platform is intended for use by persons aged 18 years or older who are KYC-compliant; we do not knowingly collect personal data of children, and where processing on behalf of a minor investor is unavoidable (e.g., guardian-operated folios), it is undertaken with verifiable consent of the parent/lawful guardian.

sections.title: 12. Marketing Communications
sections.body: We may send service, transactional and (with consent, where required) promotional communications by SMS, email, push notification or WhatsApp; you may opt out of promotional communications at any time.

sections.title: 13. Third-Party Links
sections.body: This Policy does not apply to third-party websites or apps linked from the Platform; please review their respective privacy policies.

sections.title: 14. Grievance Officer / Data Protection Contact
sections.body: For any privacy-related query, complaint or rights request, contact our Grievance Officer BINAY PRADHAN (Email: binay@eazysip.com | Phone: +91 75570 51930). We aim to acknowledge queries within 24 hours and resolve them within the timelines prescribed under applicable law.

sections.title: 15. Changes to This Policy
sections.body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time; the "last updated" date above reflects the most recent revision, and material changes will be notified through the Platform.

sections.title: 16. Governing Law
sections.body: This Policy is governed by the laws of India, subject to the jurisdiction clause in the Website Disclaimer and Terms & Conditions.
